full_report: The global market for operational AI grew 38 percent year over year in 2025. Adoption is concentrated in financial services, retail, and healthcare. Customers cite data movement and latency as the largest barriers to deployment. Vendors who co-locate inference with data are growing twice as fast as those that require ETL into a separate model serving stack. Enterprise buyers are increasingly skeptical of black-box pricing and prefer transparent per-call costs. Open-source foundation models are gaining share in privacy-sensitive verticals. We expect the trend toward in-database AI to accelerate through 2026 as more vendors expose SQL-native primitives.

Customer support automation continues to mature. Sentiment-aware routing reduces average handle time by 22 percent in deployments we benchmarked. Summarization at the agent handoff is now considered table stakes. Looking forward, the differentiator is whether the platform can operate on live ticket data without batch ETL. Companies that combine sentiment, classification and summarization in a single SQL query report the highest CSAT improvements. Concerns include hallucinations in summaries and inconsistent classification when category sets evolve over time.

Real-time fraud detection markets are bifurcating. Card-present fraud vendors compete on rule-engine speed, while card-not-present vendors increasingly rely on language models to reason over merchant descriptions. Vector similarity over user-behavior embeddings is emerging as a strong signal. Reasoning LLMs let analysts encode novel fraud patterns without retraining static models. Pricing is moving from per-transaction to per-API-call as model cost dominates the unit economics. False positive rates remain the biggest customer pain point.

Churn prediction tooling is shifting from black-box scores toward explainable, narrative outputs. Customer success teams want to know not only that a customer is at risk but why. LLM-based zero-shot classifiers, while less accurate than purpose-built models, win on time-to-value and explainability. The most successful deployments combine traditional behavioral telemetry with sentiment derived from support interactions. We expect explainable churn outputs to become a standard feature within 18 months.
